history.origins: Trijumf, also known as Croatian Triumph, is a card game popular on the Croatian coast and islands. Although the name is similar to Italian trionfo, the Croatian version is more similar to the Venetian game madrasso, with some elements of marianna.
timeline: 20th century: Popular on Croatian coast and islands; evolved from Italian ace-ten games (Briscola, Tressette).
history.cultural: The most popular card game in Dalmatia.
history.evolution: Hybrid of Briscola (trumps) and Tressette (point values).

setup.deck: 40 cards (Triestine). Rank: A-3-K-Kt-J-7-6-5-4-2. Values: A=11, 3=10, K=4, Kt=3, J=2. Total 120 + 10 for last trick = 130.
setup.dealing: 10 cards each. Trump determined by card flip or declaration.

rules.objective: The player or partnership aims to be the first to reach at least 401 card points over one or more deals; 501 is sometimes used for longer games.
rules.gameplay: Play tricks. Follow suit. Must trump if void in suit. AkuÅ¾anje: Declare K+Kt of same suit = 20 pts (40 if trump suit). Score card values. Last trick = 10 bonus.
keyRules: Must trump if void (unusual for Italian games)

strategy.basic: Play trumps to win valuable tricks. Declare when eligible.
strategy.intermediate: Coordinate with partner. Manage trump suit holdings.
strategy.advanced: Count points. Claim victory at the right moment.
tips: Aces and 3s are the most valuable cards.
